title: Long ARM Holdings — N1X Architecture Win + Windows AI PC TAM Opening
entry: Initiate $340-360 on any consolidation after today's COMPUTEX gap-up (day range $337.00–$356.45, new 52-week high at $356.45). Scale: 60% on a pullback to $340-350 early in the June 2 session; 40% add on any further dip to $330-338 or a confirmed close above $360 with above-average volume. Do NOT chase above $365 without a secondary OEM adoption catalyst (Dell, HP, Lenovo laptop lineup announcements).
stop_loss: $318 daily close (~9.1% below entry midpoint $350) — implies the N1X Windows AI PC product cycle misses Holiday 2026 OEM lineup commitments, OR the chip-curb rule expands in scope to include Arm-architecture chips, OR a broad AI semis de-rating breaks the sector thesis
targets: $385 — N1X confirmed in 2+ Windows OEM laptop lineups for Holiday 2026; ARM royalty pipeline visibility increases; +10% from entry $350
$425 — ARM Q1 FY2027 earnings (late July / early August 2026) shows licensing revenue growth accelerating above 30% YoY on N1X design wins plus smartphone AI refresh cycle; +21.4%

catalyst: NVDA's COMPUTEX 2026 keynote unveiled the N1X — the first Arm-architecture PC processor co-developed by NVIDIA, ARM Holdings, and MediaTek, designed for Windows AI PCs and shipping in Windows laptops this fall 2026. Microsoft co-announced N1X as the Windows 11 AI PC reference platform. Every N1X chip shipped earns ARM Holdings a royalty. The Windows PC market (approximately 250 million units annually) has been exclusively x86 for 30+ years — Intel and AMD have divided this TAM entirely. N1X is the first credible Arm-based Windows computing platform since the early Qualcomm Snapdragon experiments, differentiated by NVDA's AI acceleration silicon and Microsoft's Windows 11 AI optimization. ARM stock jumped +5.4% today to a new 52-week high of $356.45, reflecting the initial re-rating; the royalty pipeline visibility from OEM design wins and Q1 FY2027 earnings will drive the next leg over 2–4 months.
thesis:
ARM Holdings earns royalties on every chip that uses its Instruction Set Architecture — it does not manufacture chips but licenses the ISA and chip designs to partners. The business model creates extraordinary leverage on adoption: once an ISA standard is adopted by an OEM (as N1X is expected to be in Windows laptops), ARM earns recurring royalties on every unit shipped with no incremental capital investment. The Windows PC TAM opening is structurally unlike any prior Arm-in-PC attempt. NVDA's GPU design expertise ensures N1X AI acceleration is the best available for Windows AI workloads. Microsoft's co-development commitment ensures Windows 11 will be fully optimized for the Arm ISA. MediaTek's manufacturing relationships ensure production scale. These three partners remove the three obstacles that defeated prior Arm-PC attempts.

The royalty math is compelling. ARM earns approximately $0.10–0.15 per smartphone chip in royalties (at scale). PC chips are higher-value, commanding closer to $0.25–0.40 per unit. At 20M N1X units in the first full year (roughly 8% of the PC market at a premium price point), ARM adds approximately $5–8M in annual royalties just from N1X — modest on a $3.5B ARM annual revenue base, but the royalty percentage is closer to $50–100M at full penetration (80M+ units/year). More importantly, the market re-rates ARM's multiple when a new TAM this large becomes visible. ARM's current business is ~60% mobile, ~25% data center/cloud, ~15% IoT/automotive. Adding 250M annual PCs to the serviceable TAM expands the long-run royalty base by 30–40% at scale.

The near-term thesis is positioning ahead of OEM announcements and Q1 FY2027 earnings (late July). OEM design-win announcements typically follow COMPUTEX by 4–8 weeks as laptop manufacturers finalize their Holiday lineup reveals. Microsoft's Surface team (which co-announced N1X) will likely be the first announced customer; Dell, HP, and Lenovo are expected to follow. Each OEM announcement is a mini-catalyst that confirms the royalty pipeline. ARM's Q1 FY2027 earnings (reporting late July or early August for the April–June quarter) will contain initial guidance for N1X licensing revenue and royalty pipeline commitments.

The chip-curb rule is irrelevant to ARM Holdings directly: the Malaysia loophole closure targets NVDA Blackwell GPUs and AMD MI350x GPUs — specific chip products that Chinese entities were procuring through Malaysian intermediaries. ARM's architecture license is held by NVDA (for N1X design), not Chinese entities. The chip-curb adds a layer of relative safety to ARM as a beneficiary of the AI chip ecosystem that avoids the export restriction complexity entirely.
bull_case: N1X confirmed in the Holiday 2026 lineups of Microsoft Surface, Dell XPS, HP Spectre, and Lenovo ThinkPad by mid-July. ARM Q1 FY2027 earnings (late July) shows licensing revenue +35% YoY on N1X design wins plus data center AI chip royalties growing +50% YoY on NVDA Rubin and AMD MI400 ramp. Management raises FY2027 royalty guidance to reflect N1X. Stock re-rates from current 46x forward earnings to 55x on TAM expansion. Target 2 ($425) in sight within 8 weeks. Tail: Apple announces N1X adoption for the iPad Pro (enterprise AI use case), expanding N1X TAM by an additional 50M units/year.
bear_case: N1X fails to gain OEM traction at Holiday 2026 pricing — laptop makers can't price N1X PCs competitively against Intel/AMD at the $999-1,299 mainstream tier where volumes are. ARM's royalty from N1X is delayed to H1 2027. Simultaneously, the chip-curb rule expands to include Arm-based data center chips (Rubin, Graces), reducing ARM's data center royalty growth. Stock gives back the COMPUTEX gap and revisits $320-330. Tail: NVDA and MediaTek have a design disagreement over N1X pricing structure and delay launch to 2027, creating a 12-month gap in the N1X royalty thesis.
invalidation: $318 daily close, OR NVDA announces N1X launch delay beyond Spring 2027, OR ARM reports Q1 FY2027 licensing revenue growth below 15% YoY implying N1X design-win pipeline is thinner than expected
